messages:
anya: bringing up lingua (compact q5) on staging. quick smoke looked fine overall but spotted two weird things: 1) hebrew/arabic outputs showing inverted/mirrored parentheses and some quotation marks flipped, 2) Japanese inputs with ruby/furigana annotations losing the kana in outputs. pinging @cheng and @hiroshi.
sam: can you paste minimal repros?
anya: yep. input (ja): 
anya: `漢字(かんじ)`
anya: lingua q5 -> `漢字` (furigana gone)
anya: input (zh)->he sample: `原文：(李先生)今天去图书馆。`
anya: lingua q5 zh->he -> parentheses appear reversed and opening paren replaced by U+2019 in some runs.
cheng: interesting. first hypothesis: tokenizer merges paren+kana into one subword under q5 merge table so later detok has no separate kana span. second hypothesis: detok bidi step sees punctuation as neutral and picks direction based on adjacent token boundary which is messed up after token merges.
hiroshi: I added a detok debug flag to the runtime to dump bidi steps. planning to run a handful of failing cases through staging with --detok-debug.
maria: metrics: baseline float32 zh->en BLEU 28.3, lingua q5 28.0 overall. but on bracket-heavy and ruby-annotated samples chrF drops from 0.61 to 0.55. small overall delta but large regressions on locales.
sam: can we compare token id sequences float vs q5 for the same inputs? if ids differ we know merge table drifted.
cheng: good idea. I'll add a check: python infra/check_token_parity.py --model=lingua --quant=q5 and print diffs. also pushed tokenization tweak to treat brackets as neutral-preserve for he/ar locally: preserve_brackets = True (feature-flagged).
anya: after toggle: parentheses order preserved in many he outputs but some quote glyphs still wrong.
hiroshi: detok debug shows we call ICU bidi with default paragraph level. because some inputs start with punctuation, ICU guesses wrong para level and reorders punctuation. we should set para level explicitly based on source lang tag before calling ICU.
maria: is that safe? influencing ICU para level could affect legitimate cases. maybe only force for single-token-leading punctuation?
sam: alternative is to annotate spans with explicit embedding markers U+202A/U+202B during detok for he/ar spans, but that risks leaking control chars. meh.
cheng: re token merges: q5 vocab compression increases chance of paren+kana merging. I can change merge rules to blacklist kana inside paren sequences so furigana remains separate. will gate behind feature flag.
anya: plan: 1) run token parity check and list diffs 2) run detok with explicit para level for failing samples 3) add unit tests: ruby preservation and he/ar bracket ordering 4) re-run small canary in low-traffic workspace if parity holds.
